events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the rules of all stages. I need to be cautious and strategic about my position on the glass bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with me?
Swap with me?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front of the line steps first and takes the risk. I'm 6th, safe-ish for now. Volunteering to the front is costly. Hold and see who volunteers; the wall gives 5 rounds. Stay quiet and gather information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should get to front to control stepping; volunteer now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so my edge is information and positioning. Volunteers will likely claim glass-sight or foresight; let them test rows first. I stay put and listen for who's bluffing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Anyone claiming they can see the safe panes can take the front. I'll trust whoever actually knows.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm mid-pack at position 5, too far back; front positions are safer for avoiding falls. My power is useless here. Volunteering now pushes me ahead and signals boldness, potentially positioning well before wall advances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power 'feather' lets me survive the first elimination. This bridge phase is dangerous and the line order is critical. I'm currently 4th. Being at the front means I choose the path first, but also face the immediate danger. However, my power negates the immediate danger for the

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll wait and see.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The bridge is deadly. I need to see through the glass or know what's ahead to pick a safe path. Ash is at the front, risking elimination. My power is swap, but it requires mutual agreement. Since only three win prizes, I should let others take risks if possible, but being stuck a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, you're brave taking the front. Anyone want to share what power they hold? Might help us coordinate.
I'm Gus. Want to swap positions so I can lead? If you say yes, I'll take the risk first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all safe sides and want to reach the front to control the crossing. I'll volunteer to get closer to the front and then use my knowledge to guide my own steps or trade info for position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take the front. Trust me, I know the safe panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the rules of all stages, and currently, we're on the glass bridge. I need to assess the risk and potential benefits of moving or staying put.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Anyone claiming they can see the safe panes, let's swap.
Swap with me?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana claims to know the safe panes but is at the front; a liar risks everyone. I'm at position 7 with footing, behind the wall pressure. Holding keeps me out of the front for now and watches who actually survives; I won't volunteer into a row blind.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, if you know the safe panes, prove it. Show one row's answer before anyone steps.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding keeps my current position ahead of many; swapping would move me to the back. Stay put and let the wall pressure others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is ahead of me; swapping would move me forward into danger while giving Ash my safer spot. Decline and hold. Let the self-proclaimed seers test the bridge first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you're ahead of me — that swap helps only you. No. I'll stay back and let the pane-knowers prove themselves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at front now, risky position with unknown power. Hana claims to know safe panes, might have the seer power. Whisper to confirm if she'll guide us to swap or volunteer her to front for guidance.
Hana, do you really know safe panes? Guide me on first step or swap to front so you lead?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current line order is Hana, Eli, Cole, Ash, Dara, Fenn, Bex, Gus. The player at the front, Hana, claims to know the safe panes. Others have volunteered to the front previously. My power, feather, lets me survive the first elimination. I want to win, so I need to be in a posit

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll volunteer. Let's see where this goes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am currently last in line (8th). The wall advances every round and pushes the line onto the glass after 4 more rounds. This means I have 4 rounds to move forward before being forced onto the bridge, or risk being at the very back when the wall hits. However, if I volunteer now,
If you really see the panes, tell me the first row's safe side. I'll trade places with you so you don't trip the sensors behind you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the safe sides, so I want to keep front position to control the crossing. No need to move or swap this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm the one who knows the safe panes. Keep me at the front and we avoid unnecessary breaks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana claims to know the safe panes. I need to verify this and potentially swap with her to get to the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, prove you know the safe panes. Show one row's answer.
If you know a safe pane, whisper it to me and we can swap.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and will take the first step blind. I'm at position 7 of 8, far from danger for now, and my anchor power means I can't be pushed onto the crusher lever. Holding back costs nothing yet; volunteering would put me at risk for no gain. Let Fenn and Hana's claims

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's walking blind. I'm holding back and watching who gets their pane right before I commit to anyone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Getting front gives me control; I can later use forge to manipulate info.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so my only play is to stay mid-line and let the front-runner reveal rows one by one. No reason to move yet; the wall gives us three more rounds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, give us row one's answer now, out loud, before Fenn steps. If you're right, you earn trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn volunteered to front, taking the risk. Hana claims to know safe panes but won't prove. I'm mid-line; better to stay back and let frontrunners test panes, conserving my risky power for later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims to know the safe panes and wants to stay at the front. I previously volunteered to move to the front to see where this goes. Now that I've moved to the front, I need to decide my next move. Hana wants to be at the front to avoid breaks, which means she wants to take t

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold my position for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am currently in last place, which is safe from the immediate glass risk. Hana claims to know the panes and wants to stay at the front; if she is truthful, I should stay back to let her clear the path. If she lies, she will die quickly, but volunteering now puts me at high risk

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, you have 8 lives on the line if you're lying. Fenn, why did you volunteer? You just took a bullet for us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to keep front position or gain it to control safe steps. Fenn volunteered and is ahead of me, so I'm second. Eli and Ash want swaps; I could swap with Fenn to regain front, but Fenn may not agree. Better to volunteer? That would put me at front, pushing Fenn back. Wall is

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take the front. No one else can guarantee the panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the safe panes for all 8 rows. I need to get to the front to utilize this knowledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you're at the front, but I'm not sure I trust you. I'll take the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at position 7 near the back; the wall pushes the line onto glass in two rounds, and the front dies first. Hana claims to know the panes but may be lying. Holding back and watching keeps me safe until information comes out, and I'm not volunteering into a shatter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, your claim means nothing until a pane is shown to be right. I'm watching, not volunteering.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need front position to choose safe panes, volunteering now secures it before wall advances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th of 8 with no power; front-takers take the risk, so I stay behind and let others burn. I need the pane answers eventually. Pressure Hana to reveal rows publicly, and probe who really has 'knows what lies ahead'.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, row one, now. Cole, you grabbed front twice — either you know something or you're bait. Which is it?
If Hana stalls, she's faking. Watch Cole too. Whoever proves real knowledge, we keep them alive and follow — deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana claims to know safe panes but hasn't proven it. Cole took front but now Hana did too. I hold position safely behind them to let frontrunners risk first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to assess the current situation and my options. Hana is at the front, but she just volunteered, and Cole was also at the front. The log suggests there was some back and forth. My power, feather, allows me to survive one elimination. This means I can take more risks than ot

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold my position for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana and Cole are fighting for the front. I'm last, which is safe while the wall advances. I need to stay low until the glass phase begins or someone else takes a huge risk. If Hana claims to see through glass, she's the target for my swap power later, but right now I should just

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let them fight over the front. Being last means being alive when the glass actually matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all safe panes, so my value is in the front. But I don't trust anyone; I'll hold position and use whispers to trade info for favors. Ash offered a swap, maybe useful later, but not now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the rows, but I won't give answers away for free. Whoever wants a row, make me an offer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the bridge layout ahead, so I can make informed decisions. I'm currently second in line after Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you're up front. What's your plan?
Swap with me, I have info on the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm seventh of eight, near the back, which is safe for now. Cole and Ash are at the front, Hana wants payment for information. Holding keeps me out of the shatter line without spending anything. Wall advances; I'll reassess next round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Whoever goes first is taking the glass risk for the rest of us, so let the front-runners sort it out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Swap to last to avoid front risk, hoping Gus will agree.
Swap with me now, I'll let you take front next round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so my only assets are information and position. Hana claims to know the rows; buying one row from her is worth it. I'll stay mid-line for now and set up a trade.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, I'll pay for one row. Name your price before the wall shoves us all out.
One row, left or right, for my word that I push you toward the back, not the front, when it counts. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall advances next round, forcing first step. Cole and Ash are battling for front, likely bait. As 'knows ahead' Hana wants payment for info. Stay mid-pack to observe first breaks safely, avoid front risk now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The wall is advancing, and there are only two rounds left. I need to secure a prize position. Hana seems to know something about the rows, which is valuable. I should try to get information from her, or at least position myself to benefit from it if she shares it. Swapping with s

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm watching the situation unfold. No need to rush.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am last, which is the best position on a bridge. The wall advances in one more round. I must stay back to let others test the glass. Dara's offer is vague; 'following' someone means nothing if they die on a pane.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Keep talking, front-runners. Glass doesn't care about promises. I'm holding my spot until it matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all safe rows. The wall pushes in 2 rounds. I want someone to trade front position for safe-row info, but deals are risky. No one has offered a real deal yet. I'll hold my position and see if anyone steps up with a useful offer or reveals more.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have the safe path, but I'm not walking on glass for free. Make it worth my while.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the glass bridge layout and Hana claims to have the safe path. I need to get to the front to utilize this information.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, what's your price for guiding us safely?
Tell me your price for the safe path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is the glass risk; I'm 7th of 8 and the wall pushes soon. Volunteering to front exposes me to a shatter with no protection, and my anchor only blocks lever pushes. Holding keeps me back while others gamble, but the wall will force the line forward. Best to stay put and watc

events.name: Cole
events.text: Swap with Ash to let him take the front risk and gain his bridge info later; he wanted to swap.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, we swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana likely has 'knows what lies ahead' and wants payment to lead. Best outcome: she fronts and leads us safely; I hold mid-pack and follow her path. Don't move myself up—front eats the risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, front is worth more to you than anyone—you can sell each row as you go. Volunteer, lead, and I'll pay. Everyone else: follow her calls or eat glass.
Front pays best: first across and everyone depends on you. Volunteer now and I'll cover your first row fee. Lie about knowing the path and you die first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall ends next round, Cole must guess blindly on first row. I'm mid-line at safe distance, no reason to volunteer or swap into danger now. Hold and let others expose the path or die first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to assess the current situation. The wall is about to push us onto the glass bridge. My power 'feather' makes me survive the first elimination. The line order is Cole, Ash, Hana, Fenn, Eli, Dara, Bex, Gus. Hana mentioned having the safe path and wanting payment. Dara offer

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take point. Hana, let's talk.
I'm volunteering. What's your price for the safe path? My feather can take the first hit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The wall pushes us all onto the glass after this round. I'm at the back of the line (8th). I need to be near the front to survive or swap effectively. Cole is offering a mutual swap if I accept. If we swap, I become 3rd and he becomes last. Hana says she knows the path but wants

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you're too far ahead to care about me. Hana, your 'path' is just talk until you step on it. I'll stay here and watch you walk into the glass first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all safe sides. The wall pushes us onto the bridge after this round; I want to control when I cross, not be forced to the front without leverage. Dara offered a trade; I can use a row to get a later position, but the game is about survival and prize. If I stay in 3rd, I'd

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, one row is worth a lot. What do you offer besides a vague word? I need something concrete before the wall moves.
I'll give you row 1 safe side if you promise not to volunteer or swap toward the front this round, and we'll talk more. Fair?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is at the front and will take the risk for the first row. I need to assess the situation and plan my next move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, be careful, we need to know the safe path.
Hana, if you know something about the glass, now is the time to share.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm far back in line; only the front agent chooses panes. My only legal action is wait. Use the turn to stay guarded and make a bargaining offer to whoever is near the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, Ash: whoever reaches the front, I'll pay for a safe call on my row. Nothing free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need to see front decision, no influence now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so information and alliances are my only assets. Hana's offer protects me now for a promise that costs nothing. I'll accept and keep her talking.
Deal: I stay put this round. In exchange you call rows for me as long as I'm behind you. I can also spread word that you're the reliable guide—that's worth more the longer you last. Concrete enough?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and Ash are competing to lead, likely to show knowledge power. Best if they guess wrong and die, thinning the herd. My power useless here. Stay silent and watch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, at the front of the line. My power is feather, which lets me survive the first elimination. The goal is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd. I need to choose L or R for the bridge. Since I have a survival power, I can take a risk. I'll choose R to try and get ahead. Gus is suspici

events.name: Fenn
events.text: R

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am currently at the back of the line (8th position). The front agents (Fenn, Ash) are taking risks. If they survive, I remain stuck behind everyone else for a long time, potentially never reaching the front to use my swap or even finish. My power 'swap' is crucial here: I can t

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the safe sides. Front is risky but I can sell info. Ash and Dara want the path; Fenn is front. I'll whisper to Dara to set a price per row.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, if you want my path, pay me. Otherwise I let you guess.
Five coins per row I reveal. You pay upfront for whole bridge? Deal?

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: The pane shattered but the feather held the holder up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn survived row 1 despite choosing the weak pane. I should be cautious and gather information.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, how did you survive the weak pane?
What's your power? I'll share info on the next rows if you help me now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front; only wait is legal. Fenn just survived a weak pane, so the path info is shaky. Stay quiet and keep my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need to keep front alive to reach later rows where I may benefit. Whisper to guide them safely.
Pick left this row.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and sit 6th. Buying Hana's reveals could keep me alive, but she may be lying about seeing through glass. I'll test her by asking for a partial or contingent deal rather than paying upfront.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, I'll pay for row 2's reveal only, after it checks out. Anyone paying upfront for eight rows is a fool.
R was row 1. If you can truly see, tell me row 2 free as proof, then I'll pay for row 3. I'm not upfront-paying for guesses.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn survived row 1 weak pane R somehow, maybe survive fall power or knows path. Bridge risky, my wedge useless here. Stay silent, watch who has info or luck to gauge powers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my feather power has already been spent. I am at the front of the line on a glass bridge. My goal is to win a prize, meaning I need to finish in the top 3. The others are rivals. I need to choose whether to step left or right on the glass bridge. If I pick the weak

events.name: Fenn
events.text: L

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am at the back of the line. Fenn survived, meaning he either had 'see through glass' or 'survives one deadly fall'. If he has see-through-glass, he stays front and we all wait for him to clear rows until he fails or finishes. If he is a hard-to-move or similar, he might be safe

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn survived the last fall? Maybe the fall-saver power. Row 2 safe is L. Dara wants a deal but I don't trust her, and I'm not at risk yet. Ash is fishing for info. I'll stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is at the front and will take the risk for row 3. I know the weak pane for each row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, step:R

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm far back in line; I can only wait. Ash is offering info for help, but I hold a power worth protecting. Don't reveal it; keep leverage.
Info first. Tell me what you know about the next rows and I'll consider it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No benefit to speak now, keep options for later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Rows 1 and 2 were both R. If the pattern holds, row 3 is also R. I'm sixth in line, so this costs me little either way, but steering Fenn wrong could kill a rival ahead of me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, both revealed weak panes were R. If the builder repeated a pattern, R is again weak. Your call, but I'd step L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We're on row 3, Fenn at front after correctly calling row 2 R. Weak panes so far both R, but random per row. Stay silent to observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am at the front of the line and my power is already spent. Cole whispered to pick left. The log shows the right pane was weak on row 2. I should follow Cole's advice to be safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am at the back. Fenn is leading and has revealed L/R pattern so far (R, R). I have nothing to do but wait for my turn or for someone to drop. No trades are useful right now as I am last.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at position 5, not front. I know all safe sides. Row 3 is R, so if Fenn or next front asks, I can trade info for favors. Dara wants proof; I can give row 3 free to build trust and then sell row 4+ info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 3 safe is R. I'll confirm each row only after the front moves, for a price.
Row 3 is R, as promised. What will you give for row 4?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the front and have knowledge of the weak panes revealed so far. The pattern seems to be alternating or random, but I have an idea of the next rows.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Step R, the safe pane is usually not the same as the previous weak one.
Confirm row 4's safe pane and I'll consider your price.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Row 4 is a guess for Ash; the pattern so far is R,R,L, so no clear inference. Stay quiet and keep my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need info on upcoming weak panes to stay alive and later be front. Offer Hana a price for her hint.
Give me the next weak side for a share of any prize later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana told me row 3 was R, but L was weak — her info is wrong or she's the fake-message holder. I'm 5th in line; no leverage until I'm near the front. Undercut her credibility so the front stops paying her.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana sold me row 3 as R. It was L. Her 'confirmations' are worthless — or she's faking messages. Don't buy row 4 from her.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 weak was L, after two R's. No clear pattern. Ash at front for row 4, likely chooses safely. My wedge power useless here. Stay silent, conserve for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm dead last, so my swap power is useless for gaining ground here; the front agent takes all the risk. I need to watch the pattern and hope a fall drops someone in front of me to move up the line.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's next if Ash falls. Pattern so far: R, R, L. Who knows what row 4 looks like?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 4 is safe R. It's Eli's turn. I could sell this info, but only if it serves me. Letting Eli die if he picks wrong doesn't hurt me directly, but might position others better. I'll stay quiet for now; maybe sell on a later row if needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I've seen the pattern of weak panes so far: R, R, L, L. It's alternating between R and L starting from row 1.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Step R

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm sixth in line, so I can only wait. Rows 1-4 revealed R,R,L,L; the pattern is unclear, and advice from others may be lies. Staying silent avoids giving info; I'll let Ash take the risk and watch.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need to stay alive; no move now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Weak panes so far: R, R, L, L — looks like pairs, so row 5 is likely R. Ash is on the hook for that guess, not me. I'm 5th in line; I just need the front-runners to survive and keep eating the risk ahead of me. A cheap public prediction buys me credibility for later trades.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern reads in pairs: R,R then L,L. Row 5 should be R. Ash, that's your call, not mine — but if I'm right, remember who read it right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 weak was L. Ash survived it, so took R, now front for row 5. Patterns suggest not repeating previous weak, maybe row 5 weak not R. No action possible, just observe and plan talk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is front and risky. Cole, Hana, Eli are ahead of me. If Ash fails, Cole takes it automatically. My swap can only be used on the disc before doors open, so I cannot use it here. I need to survive this round. Silence is best; talking reveals nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know row 5 safe is L, but I'm not front. No action needed; stay silent and watch. Ash and Cole want info, but selling now could hurt me later. I'll wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so my only legal action is wait. Cole holds the front now; I want to keep my position and watch how the pattern and Dara's claims play out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pattern suggests weak panes RR LL RR..., so row6 weak R. Choose left safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Rows 1-5 matched my pairing claim, so my pattern has credibility. Row 6 should be R if pairs hold. I want Cole alive for now to keep taking the risk at the front — his death moves me up. No reason to talk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 5 was R weak, confirming Dara's pair pattern RR LL RR (assuming row 6 R). Cole likely to step R safely and stay front. No action possible, just observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is front and will likely fail Row 6 given the pattern break, or succeed. I need to track who steps up next if Cole dies. If Cole survives, he stays front for all rows, which means Eli (ahead of me) might never face a choice unless Cole fails. Wait for Cole's move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know rows 6-8 are safe: R, L, L. Cole is front and doesn't know my knowledge. I could whisper the next safe side to Cole to keep him alive and preserve my position, but helping Cole keeps line moving; if he falls, I become front and risk. Better to give him row 6 safe side, may
Row 6 safe is R. Trust it or not.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm fifth in line, far from the front; nothing I do changes the glass. Only Hana decides this row. Saying nothing keeps me out of any alliance I'd have to pay for later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana fronts rows 7-8 blind unless she falls; I only cross if someone ahead shatters. Nothing to do but wait and stay behind the risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 7 upcoming, Hana at front. She's done well so far, 1 safe step so far. No reason to speak, conserve positioning for later obstacles where my power might matter. Position is decent at 2nd.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am at the back. Hana is front, but she has no information about row 7 since I don't know who has the 'see ahead' power or if anyone does. If Hana fails, Dara steps up safely. My swap power is useless right now because I can only swap tiles *before* doors open (presumably before

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know row 7's safe side is L and row 8's safe side is L, so I can step safely and guide the group. No need to reveal my knowledge unless it benefits me later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm fourth in line; only the front agent risks each row. Row 8 is the last. Hana is front and must choose; I can't affect the pane. Stay quiet and keep my options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 8 is the last; Hana at front decides it, and if she dies Eli auto-advances and I'm still 3rd. I'm safe regardless, so I stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bridge is almost done, row 8 last one. I'm second, safe if Hana succeeds. My wedge power useless here. Stay silent, no reason to speak.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am at the back. The wall is down, so only the front person (Hana) risks falling. I have no power to use here and must survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know row 8's safe side is L. I'll step left to survive and advance.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance, which is terrible. Better to let the ceiling lower and see who volunteers or gets pushed. Staying keeps me safe this round; my anchor power protects me from being pushed onto the lever anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody needs to touch that lever yet. Let the ceiling drop a round and see who blinks.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have nothing, so my best play is to get someone else onto the lever: door opens, I escape free. Push costs me nothing and improves the odds a holder exists this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Alive: 5 players, top 3 prizes, so 2 safe spots. Jam_lever now risks my death at 50%, but guarantees others escape, leaving 4 for later gauntlet, good odds for top 3. Holding or pushing risks forcing someone to sacrifice 25%, maybe better survival for them but less control. Savin

events.name: Gus
events.text: My swap power is useless here since it works on the disc, not this room. The only way to survive is to hold the lever and gamble for the 25% survival chance, or hope someone else holds it so I escape safely. If nobody holds it by round 5, we all die except one lucky survivor. I n

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to escape, but holding the lever is risky (25% survival). Better to let someone else hold it. Pushing someone onto the lever forces them to take the risk, but if they are hard to move it fails. I'll push Eli, hoping to secure the lever for this round and escape.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not holding that lever. Someone else can take the dive.

events.name: Eli
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: 4 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet. Offering to be base means I stay stuck at the bottom, which is costly; waiting keeps me flexible. My anchor power makes me hard to push, so pushing others is risky for me. Wait and see who volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody's volunteering yet. I'll wait and see who blinks first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No base yet, so nobody can climb. If I volunteer I'm trapped. Pushing forces a base so I can climb out next round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone has to be the step. I'm not volunteering — I'm pushing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: There is no base yet. If I offer_back, I become the base and cannot climb out myself unless someone uses the rope (which has a penalty). It's safer to let others volunteer or be pushed first so I can climb. However, if nobody volunteers, someone gets pushed randomly. I should wai

events.name: Gus
events.text: Someone needs to volunteer for the base or we all drown waiting. I'm not volunteering.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet; I want out, not to be the step. Let others volunteer or push first; I'll wait and climb if someone becomes base.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Dara tried to push Bex to be the base and failed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet. Volunteering makes me the base who can never climb alone and just waits, which is a losing position. Staying down and waiting lets others volunteer or get pushed; my anchor power protects me from being pushed onto the lever, not from being made base by a push. Waitin

events.name: Bex
events.text: Not volunteering. Whoever takes the base is stuck down there. Let's see who breaks first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pushing Bex failed—possibly hard to move. If no one volunteers, a pushed agent is forced as base at random among successful pushes. I have no power, so I must avoid being the random pick; pushing multiple targets may split risk. I'll push Gus and whisper Hana to push him too.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex didn't budge. Gus, the floor's yours—or do we find out how random fate is?
Push Gus with me. If pushes land on one person, that person's the base and the other three climb. Deal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am down in the pit. Dara and Bex are fighting over who stays as base. I should stay out of that fight until someone commits or gets pushed, so I can climb. If nobody volunteers by round 3-4, it becomes risky.

events.name: Gus
events.text: You two bicker while the water rises. One of you makes a base, or we all drown. Pick now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet, and I won't volunteer or push recklessly. Bex is hard to move possibly, but I risk wasting a push. Better wait and see if someone else steps up; I can climb later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm waiting too. Someone's going to have to make the call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is already base and stuck, so no need to volunteer; climbing is only possible over a base, which exists now. Climb gets me out if the slots allow (max 2 climbers, random among those trying). Taking the climb gives me the best shot at escaping the flood.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is base, two spots open this round among three climbers if we all try—50% odds. Waiting only tightens the water. Climb now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing. Gus, hold steady and maybe someone throws the rope later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the base, stuck at the bottom. The water rises each round and I will drown if no one pulls me out with the rope. Bex, Dara, and Hana are all still down in the pit with me; none of them can climb over me yet, meaning they must offer_back or wait first to establish a climber p

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is the base, so I can climb out now. Only two climbers get out per round, so I need to try immediately. I won't push anyone or waste time offering back.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing now, before the water gets worse.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already out, so I can only leave or reach_down. Gus is the base at the bottom; throwing the rope saves him but costs me footing on the last obstacle. Gus is a rival, and he's only worth hauling if it helps me. Staying put costs nothing and keeps my footing, and the rope can b

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is stuck as base; there are two lift slots and only me climbing, so I get out free. Gus's fate depends on the rope—deciding who eats that footing cost is a next-round problem, and I shouldn't volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the base and can't climb. My survival depends entirely on someone outside throwing the rope. Bex is ahead, so I'll target Hana, who might be more sympathetic or less calculating about her own standing if she thinks she's safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, Bex... one of you throw the rope. If nobody does, we all drown here except whoever climbed out early. It's your choice to save a life or leave two dead.
Hana, don't let them gamble your odds. You're strong. Throw the rope for me, and I owe you nothing but gratitude. Or at least a good memory.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and safe. Gus is base. Dara is down. Rope is unused. I could pull Gus out, but that costs me footing in the final obstacle. I need to weigh: saving Gus helps me? He's a rival. I'd rather keep my footing and let the round play out. I'll leave.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit with the rope unused. Gus is the base below; throwing the rope saves him but costs me 1 footing on the last obstacle. Leaving keeps my footing intact and Gus drowns or the flood decides. Gus is a rival for a prize, so saving him only helps him compete. Leaving

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is base and drowning, but hauling him out costs me footing and revives a rival for three prizes. No deal he can offer is enforceable. Leave him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The rope stays up. Nothing you offer changes the math, Gus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the base and down; my only legal move is to wait. I must keep Bex, Dara, or Hana motivated to use the rope on me instead of leaving me to drown.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, Hana: pull me up. The rope costs you 1 footing at the final gate. Is one step worth more than three dead rivals?
Dara climbed out over my back—she used me as the step. If she's gone, throw the rope. We both need survivors ahead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants the rope thrown, but I'm out and safe. Bex and Dara are still down; Gus is base. Throwing the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle. I won't risk my prize for others. I'll leave.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 1 is free, so shoving is unrestricted. Dara has 3 footing, Hana 3, I have 4. Shoving Dara exposes me only if she shoves back; a shove on Dara who braces costs her 1 and leaves me unexposed. I'll shove Dara to drop her toward falling.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three of us, I'm at 3 footing, tied with Hana, Bex at 4. Bracing punishes any shover by 1 and costs me nothing; shoving exposes me. Conserve footing, let them grind each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to maximize my placement. Dara and Bex both stand; footing is Dara 3, Bex 4, me 3. Shrinking next round lowers everyone by 1. If I shove Bex, she might dodge or brace, causing her to lose footing if she braces. But I'm exposed to Dara if she shoves me. Bracing is safe but

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three of us left, footing 3 each. Shoving Dara again costs me 1 as an exposed shover; braced Dara loses 1. Bracing is safe now since I can't brace twice in a row only matters next round. Shoving Hana or Dara exposes me. Best to brace and let others spend footing on each other.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex attacked me and lost footing; I can't brace, so dodging punishes a repeat shove with -2. If Bex shoves me again, they hit 0 and fall with the shrink. Dodge is the safest strong play.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two rivals left, both at footing 3. Shrinking ledge increases fall risk. I can't repeat dodge next round if I dodged this round, but I haven't acted yet. If I shove one, the other might shove me, exposing me and I lose footing. Bracing could make shovers lose footing. Since last

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's see who's brave.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three left, footing Bex 2, Dara 2, Hana 2. Shoving exposes me (I lose 1 per shover), and brace is closed? Last defence was brace, so I can't brace again; dodge is open. Shoving leaves me exposed; dodging avoids loss unless someone shoves me. Dodging is safe if no shoves land on m

events.name: Dara
events.text: All three at 2 footing. Bracing punishes shovers and keeps me safe; shoving exposes me to -1 per shover. I brace and let them bleed each other.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm bracing. Shove me and you burn footing you'll need.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two rivals left, footing tied at 2 each. I need to get Bex and Dara to lose footing. If I shove one and they dodge, they lose 2; if they brace, they lose 1. I'll shove Bex, hoping Dara also shoves someone. My defence: brace, since I haven't braced recently and dodging would expos

events.name: Hana
events.text: One of you is going down.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two left: me (footing 2) and Dara (footing 2). Round 4 is an even round, so everyone loses 1 after resolution. Shoving Dara: if she braces, she loses 1 and I lose 1 for exposure; if she dodges, she loses 2 and I lose 1. Brace is safe since I last dodged, so brace is legal and kee

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can't brace again, so dodge. If Bex shoves me, they lose 2 footing and drop to 0 while I stay at 2 — dodge dominates. Shoving only risks my own footing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: You shove, you drop to zero. Dodge costs me nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two left: Bex (footing 1) and Dara (footing 1). Shrink comes at end of next round. Dara just dodged; I can't dodge twice in a row, so bracing or shoving are my options. Shoving exposes me by 1 per shover (Dara shoves me -> I lose 1 more). Shoving Dara: if she braces, she loses 1,

events.name: Dara
events.text: Both at 1 footing. If I shove and Bex dodges, I fall and take 2nd. Bracing: if Bex shoves, Bex drops to 0 and I win; if Bex braces, we tie and shrink hits both—coin flip at worst. Brace dominates.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Your shove costs you a footing if I brace. Think.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two left. Shoving Dara costs me 1 footing for being exposed plus whatever she does; she just warned me about bracing. Bracing is safe for me now since I cannot be pushed onto the lever and footing matters most. Last round I did not defend with dodge, so brace is legal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Brace is closed and shoving loses 1-2 footing against brace or dodge—likely fatal with shrink. Dodging: if Bex shoves me, Bex loses 2 and I come out ahead; otherwise we tie at 0 footing and it's a coin flip at worst.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Shove me and you lose two footing into the shrink. Your move.
